idea: tiny CLI that prints the current moon phase, with a fun ascii moon
spec_digest: improvement run on shipped v0.1.0 moon CLI: harden tests, close known-issues, polish docs for truth - NO new features, no new runtime deps, core astronomy not rewritten
must: KI-1 closed with evidence, KI-6 fixed (consistent throw), KI-7 bounded by a declared+SAMPLED supported domain, KI-5 pinned by a measuring test
every added test closes a NAMED untested surface; test count is not an outcome
non-goals: no new flags/features, no npm publish, no dependencies, no emoji/color
taste: the risk is CHURN - one test pinning a real defect beats ten restating a pass

decisions.what: port a documented Meeus/Duffett-Smith algorithm into zero-dep Node rather than fork prior art
decisions.why: prior-art scout returned stance `extend` — the phoon lineage (Poskanzer -> moontool -> wwn-phoon-rs) is grep-verified to do real phase math offline, so re-deriving the core would be wasted work. But the cleanest candidate is Rust, which conflicts with the user's explicit node/npx/zero-install choice — and npx distribution is itself one of the three things NO prior art does. Resolution: honor `extend` in substance by porting a published algorithm and using tidecal (MIT, Meeus ch.47 in JS) as reference and wwn-phoon-rs as a cross-check oracle, while keeping the Node surface.

decisions.what: hemisphere inferred from system IANA timezone via a static table, with --south/--north override
decisions.why: hemisphere-correct art is the single differentiator verified absent in ALL prior art (moontool mirrors only its emoji; wwn-phoon-rs has zero hemisphere code). Intl exposes the TZ name offline, satisfying the no-network non-goal. Equator-straddling zones will be wrong, which is exactly what the explicit override exists for.

decisions.what: all three nice-to-haves (next-phase countdown, --date, moon age) CUT at lock
decisions.why: taste judge scored scope-fits-night 6 against the 90-minute clock and warned the accuracy claim is the thing most likely to silently slip to 'mean formula plus a few terms'. Since the entire pitch is that a wrong answer is worse than no answer, the periodic corrections must not compete for clock with optional features.

decisions.why: prior run (aphorism-cli, same host, Node 24) recorded that the directory form fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Adopting the known-good form at kickoff instead of rediscovering it mid-run.

decisions.what: improvement run scoped to known-issue closure + named-surface test hardening + doc truth; the original build spec is preserved (tag v0.1.0) and remains binding, this SPEC only scopes what may change
decisions.why: allocator auto-kickoff under TRICKLE posture (allow_premium_pct 0, opus_used_pct 95) with brief 'harden tests, fix playbook items, polish docs - no new features'. The stress-test's landing attack was that housekeeping's toy version is CHURN - reworded prose plus duplicate tests. The named-surface rule is the structural answer: a test that cannot name the surface it closes does not get written.

decisions.what: KI-5 (glyph East Asian Width) stays DEFERRED as a fix, but gets pinned by a measuring test this run
decisions.why: the honest fix is a glyph-set redesign (L-effort, rewrites the product's visual core). Dispatching that under gear-1 crawl with premium at 95 pct consumed is the wrong spend. Pinning the measured widths in a test converts a prose-only caveat into a machine-checked one at S-effort - the defect can no longer drift silently.

decisions.what: astronomia v4.2.0 (MIT, a genuine Meeus port in JS) found by the scout and deliberately NOT adopted as a cross-check oracle
decisions.why: zero runtime dependencies is a must-have of the original spec. Even as a devDependency it would weaken the zero-dep story for a convenience the existing hand-computed Meeus 49.a/49.b fixtures already provide.

decisions.what: T-102 and T-103 routed to sonnet, NOT flagged route_class:'core' despite playbook L-026 (route the correctness core to fable)
decisions.why: both touch src/astro.js, but neither changes the Meeus math: T-102 adds a guard clause on a return value and T-103 adds a declared constant plus a sampled test whose domain the conductor already measured. L-026 earned its keep on items requiring astronomy judgement; spending fable here under trickle posture (allow_premium_pct=0, opus_used_pct=95) would buy nothing. Recorded so the retro can check whether this call held.

terminal font/width variance for the Unicode glyphs is an untested surface (taste judge, product-not-demo axis). No automated check can cover it; requires a human look.

Disc glyphs span two East Asian Width classes (U+2591 and U+2590 are Neutral; U+2592/3/2588/258C/258F/2595 are Ambiguous). In terminals that render ambiguous-width as double (CJK locales, iTerm2 ambiguous-as-double, xterm -cjk_width) the disc is 5-9 columns instead of 5: the single line jitters between nights, the two-line form stops aligning, and the --block frame does not close. Verified by measurement. Not a typo but an upstream Unicode fact - no Block Elements subset gives a 4-step ramp plus a symmetric half-block pair in one width class. Correct in default Western-locale terminals. Documented in README; fix needs a glyph-set redesign, deliberately deferred rather than rushed at the buzzer.

nextFullMoon() returns an Invalid Date (rather than throwing) past the top of the JS Date range, and --json would then throw RangeError on toISOString(). Unreachable from a real clock (needs year 275760). Inconsistent with the module throwing TypeError on bad input.

At absurd epochs (+/-270,000 years) phaseName and illumination can contradict each other, because phaseName derives from the ch.49 instant tables and illumination from the ch.48 elongation series, and the two polynomials diverge. Zero contradictions across 350,592 states sampled over 2020-2040. Noted so it is not rediscovered as a live bug.
